gappers.catalyst: Oppenheimer initiated coverage today (Nov 19) at Outperform with a $30 price target, ~3x spot — the only fresh sell-side initiation on the list.
headlines: Oppenheimer initiates Unusual Machines at Outperform, $30 target (Nov 19)
Q3 revenue $13.9M, +551% y/y, net loss $25.0M (-$0.50/sh), mostly non-cash (Nov 5)
Nov 13 registration statement covers 1.93M holder shares (resale, not new capital)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Oppenheimer opened coverage this morning at Outperform with a $30 target, roughly 3x the current price, citing UMAC's position as a parts supplier to defense primes and growth tied to US Army drone procurement. It lands on a stock that has been cut down hard: UMAC trades at $10.49 against a 52-week range of $7.25-$34.93, and the two prior analyst actions both went the other way (Needham cut to $22 from $40 on Nov 6, Piper Sandler trimmed to $27 on Nov 9). Fundamentals are a genuine split: Q3 revenue was $13.9M, up 551% from $2.1M a year earlier, but the company lost $25.0M (-$0.50/share), which management attributed mostly to non-cash items. The largest disclosed order remains the $16.9M Powerus purchase order from October.
gappers.why: A fresh initiation at ~3x spot on a heavily de-rated small cap is a sentiment-repair trigger, not new business information. Nothing about UMAC's revenue or backlog changed overnight; what changed is that a sell-side desk put a 3x target on a name sitting 70% below its 52-week high, which pulls in momentum buyers and squeezes shorts in a thin float. The move is amplified by the broad risk-on reversal in high-beta defense/drone names.
gappers.impact: Volume confirms real repositioning rather than a thin print — 791k by 10:09 ET against a 20-day IEX average of 107k is roughly 7.4x, among the heaviest participation on the list. But the driver is an opinion, not a contract, and the Needham/Piper cuts show how fast sell-side sentiment on this name reverses. The Nov 13 resale registration for 1.93M holder shares is live overhead supply. Sector read-through is limited: the drone/defense complex is moving with the general high-beta bid rather than on a shared catalyst.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: An analyst initiation is a re-rating of opinion with no durable operational change, and the $25.0M quarterly loss plus live resale supply gives the bounce nothing structural to hold; expect it to fade without follow-through news.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Cannot be sized to the rulebook. ATR(14) is $1.30, or 13.6% of price, so the mandatory 10% trailing stop at $9.44 sits at 0.73 ATR — inside a single average day's range, meaning routine noise stops the trade out. Placing the stop at a sane 1 ATR ($9.19) is 12.4% away and breaks the 10% rule. A 2:1 target off the 10% stop is $12.59, which is reachable against the $30 target and the $34.93 high, so reward is not the problem; stop placement disqualifies it. With zero open positions nothing existing is displaced, so the real cost is one of three weekly trade slots (0/3 used, week of Nov 16) spent on the weakest-quality catalyst here — an opinion — while KLIC and QCOM at ranks 6-7 are the only two names today whose volatility actually fits the 10% stop.

gappers.catalyst_detail: There is no CoreWeave-specific announcement dated today. The move is the AI-infrastructure complex repairing after four consecutive down sessions. Two inputs drive it: Nvidia's fiscal Q3, which roughly doubled revenue to more than $115B with net profit of $65.3B and beat expectations, and the Anthropic IPO pricing above its range at $83/share with a debut at 09:30 ET today. Notably the tape refused to reward the Nvidia print on Nov 18 — WSJ reported blockbuster earnings 'failed to give tech stocks much of a lift' and Bloomberg noted stocks closed lower for a fourth straight session — so today is the delayed reaction. CoreWeave's own last discrete catalyst was its Nov 10 Q3: revenue $3.66B, up 168% y/y, alongside an upsized ~$4.2B convertible note raise.
gappers.why: CoreWeave is the most liquid pure-play proxy on AI compute demand, so it trades as a leveraged expression of AI capex sentiment. Nvidia's print is the upstream demand signal and Anthropic's above-range pricing independently validates the scale of the compute buildout CoreWeave rents capacity for. The mechanism is a short-covering reversal in an oversold high-beta name once two confirming datapoints removed the demand-doubt that drove the four-day selloff.
gappers.impact: Participation is the strongest on the list and genuinely heavy — 13.36M shares by 10:09 ET against a 20-day IEX average of 1.49M is roughly 9x — which reads as real institutional repositioning, not a headline spike. The catalyst is also fundamentally anchored rather than cosmetic. Two offsets: the stock is moving on someone else's news, and the Anthropic debut is an unpriced event happening during today's session, so the driver is not yet settled. Read-through is broad and confirmed across the neocloud and AI-power complex — BE, RGTI and QBTS are all gapping on the same risk-on impulse — which means this is effectively one macro trade expressed many ways on today's list.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The underlying thesis is structural — 168% y/y revenue growth against contracted AI-compute demand, and Technology sits in the favored early-cycle bucket of the rotation table — but today's specific gap is sentiment, so the hold case rests on the backlog, not the headline.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Best-confirmed gap today on volume and the cleanest macro logic, and it still fails the stop rule. ATR(14) is $6.01, or 12.6% of price, so the 10% trail at $46.57 sits at 0.80 ATR — stopped out by four-fifths of an average day's range. A 1-ATR stop at $45.73 is 11.6% away, outside the 10% rule. A 2:1 target off the 10% stop is $62.09, below the pre-selloff range and credible, so reward clears and structure does not. At $51.74 the 20% equity cap ($20,000) allows 386 shares, so sizing is not the binding constraint. The honest cost is factor concentration: CRWV, BE, RGTI and QBTS are the same risk-on AI-infrastructure bet, so taking CRWV should rule out the others under the correlation gate rather than stacking four correlated names into a 6-position book. Entering before the Anthropic debut prices in also means buying the catalyst at peak uncertainty.

headlines: HC Wainwright trims FY2026 loss estimate to -$1.09 from -$1.03 (Nov 19)
Phase 2 FREEDOM2-DM1: 46.5% mean splicing correction at 10 mg/kg vs 6.8% placebo; stock nearly doubled premarket (Nov 10)
$125M offering priced at 25M shares at $5.00, plus 30-day option for 3.75M more (~Nov 11)
gappers.catalyst_detail: No new PepGen news is dated today beyond an estimate revision — HC Wainwright trimmed its FY26 loss estimate to -$1.09 from -$1.03. The live catalyst is still the Nov 10 Phase 2 FREEDOM2-DM1 readout in myotonic dystrophy type 1, where the 10 mg/kg arm showed 46.5% mean splicing correction versus 6.8% for placebo and the stock nearly doubled premarket. PepGen immediately monetized that move with a $125M offering: 25M shares priced at $5.00 with a 30-day underwriter option for 3.75M more, on top of $104.8M of existing cash. Two material caveats sit under the data — it covers only six treated patients, and a US clinical hold remains in place. Price targets went up after the readout (Wedbush $4 to $10 Outperform, Guggenheim $7 to $15 Buy, BofA upgraded to Neutral at $6), but the stock round-tripped from ~$5 back to a $3.83 close.
gappers.why: This is post-offering mean-reversion churn in a low-priced biotech, not a new catalyst. The $5.00 offering reset the float and handed 25M new shares to buyers whose cost basis is $5.00, so the stock is oscillating beneath a fixed, identifiable supply shelf. A 7.8% move on a $4 stock is less than one average daily range for this name, so the 'gap' is substantially noise amplified by the general risk-on tape.
gappers.impact: Reads as a one-day headline-free spike likely to mean-revert, and volume agrees — 570k by 10:09 ET against a 20-day IEX average of 251k is about 2.3x, the weakest relative participation of the top five by a wide margin. A six-patient dataset with an unresolved US clinical hold is not a durable thesis, and the offering has already converted the good news into cash and dilution. No sector read-through: no peer is moving on this, confirming it is idiosyncratic drift rather than a thesis.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: No news today, the Phase 2 readout is nine days stale and already monetized via the offering, and the next real information event is clinical rather than scheduled — nothing to carry a position into.
gappers.opportunity_cost: This is the third straight session PEPG has screened as a gapper and the conclusion has not changed; yesterday's TRADE-LOG already recorded it as FAIL. Two independent gates kill it. First, R:R: the 2:1 target off a 10% stop is $4.96, which lands almost exactly on the $5.00 offering price — the single heaviest block of overhead supply in the stock — so the trade must fight through 25M shares at breakeven cost to reach its target. Second, stop placement: ATR(14) is $0.51, or 13.4% of price, so the 10% trail at $3.72 sits at 0.75 ATR, inside one average day's range. Note this corrects a stale reading — size.mjs reports PEPG at $2.47, which is wrong and understates ATR as a share of price; the stale-price defect was already logged in the 08:09 run and is confirmed again here. Taking it would burn one of three weekly slots on the lowest-conviction name on the board while displacing nothing, since there are no open positions. Research-only conclusion: carried forward as FAIL, no new information.

gappers.catalyst: Oversold bounce in AI-power infrastructure on the Anthropic IPO pricing above range, after a ~34% drawdown; underlying NTT DATA 900MW and Google Wyoming 702MW deals are real but previously announced.
headlines: Anthropic IPO priced above range at $83/share, debuts 09:30 ET today — AI-power read-through
NTT DATA to deploy 900MW of Bloom solid oxide fuel cell systems (Nov 5)
Bloom to build fuel cells for 702MW plant powering Google's Wyoming datacenter
Fell 4% Nov 17 as fuel-cell selloff deepened (FuelCell -5%, Plug -4%)
gappers.catalyst_detail: The proximate trigger is sector-wide rather than company-specific: the Anthropic IPO priced above its range at $83/share and debuts at 09:30 ET today, reviving AI-power suppliers after a brutal drawdown. Bloom fell roughly 34% from mid-October into Tuesday, including a ~17% decline in the past week and a 4% fall on Nov 17 as a broad fuel-cell selloff hit FuelCell (-5%) and Plug (-4%), with reporting tying the damage to post-midterm concern that policy shifts could slow domestic datacenter development. Bloom's own fundamentals are strong but already public: NTT DATA agreed on Nov 5 to deploy 900MW of its solid oxide fuel cell systems, Bloom will build the fuel cells for a 702MW plant powering Google's Wyoming datacenter, and Barclays upgraded the stock to Overweight on stronger-than-expected demand. The bear case is cash burn, which Wall Street has consistently punished.
gappers.why: The Anthropic pricing is a direct demand-signal read-through, not a sentiment accident. Above-range pricing validates the scale of the compute buildout, and the binding physical constraint on that buildout is grid power — precisely what Bloom sells, on a deploy-in-months rather than years timeline. The mechanism is therefore repair of a policy-driven overreaction: the selloff priced a slowdown in domestic datacenter development, and a landmark AI IPO pricing above range contradicts that premise.
gappers.impact: Partly sustainable, and the best fundamental anchor of the top five, because unlike UMAC or PEPG the backlog behind it is contracted and named. Volume supports it — 3.39M by 10:09 ET versus a 20-day IEX average of 552k, roughly 6x. Two real offsets: cash burn is unresolved and is the specific reason the stock has been sold, and the catalyst is an unpriced event, since Anthropic actually debuts during this session. Read-through is unambiguous and confirmed — CRWV is gapping on the identical driver and the fuel-cell group has traded as one block all week — which cuts both ways, since it means Bloom is not moving on its own merits today.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The 900MW NTT DATA deployment and the 702MW Google Wyoming plant are structural contracted demand rather than headline events, and the Technology/Industrials pairing is the favored early-cycle combination in the rotation table.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Strongest fundamental case on the board and still not sizeable under the rules. ATR(14) is $20.31, or 11.9% of price, so the 10% trail at $165.01 sits at 0.84 ATR — inside a single average day's range — while a 1-ATR stop at $163.03 is 11.1% away and breaks the rule. A 2:1 target off the 10% stop is $220.01, plausible against the pre-drawdown range, so reward clears and stop geometry does not. At $183.35 the 20% cap ($20,000) buys 109 shares, so sizing is not binding. BE competes directly with CRWV for the same Anthropic/AI-capex exposure and the correlation gate makes them substitutes, not additions — taking both would put two slots of a 6-position book into one factor. The clearest cost here is timing, not selection: entering ahead of the Anthropic debut means paying for the catalyst at peak uncertainty, and waiting for the event to price costs nothing on a LONG_TERM thesis.
